title: Choose the visual world for Postmortem
question: The roll assigned The Training File. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Training File
options.lineage: a coach's card file of positions: index cards, pressboard dividers, red pencil
options.thesis: Every mistake gets filed as a card, and the card box shows which habits keep coming back.
options.viewport: Review: board at the left; the current move is a white index card at the right with a red header rule, the mark stamped in its corner and the why typed on its lines. Critical moments stand up as tabs along the move list.
options.risk: If the card motif turns into decoration instead of structure, it gets twee. It has to stay as quick to scan as a plain analysis board.

raised.raise: Insights opens on one dominant divider: the most frequent error pattern's colour owns the top of the screen, not a thin accent.
Length is real time: each move row carries a bar measuring the seconds spent on it, from the clock data the game already has.
Colour is quarantined: move-quality colour lives only on marks and tabs, everything else is graphite ink.
The games list is a strict ruled ledger; a review finishing re-stamps its row in place and never reflows the grid.
One diagram drawing at every scale: the board, a card's diagram and an insight thumbnail share the same squares and pieces.

options.label: The Annotated Game Book
options.lineage: Chess Informant and tournament books: figurine notation, diagrams, !! and ?? symbols
options.thesis: Your game, printed and annotated like a master's game in a book.
options.viewport: Review: a two-column book spread, with the diagram inset in the commentary column and the move list read as running notation, annotations inline.
options.risk: Familiar: it's close to the current look and to where most runs in this category land.

options.label: Carbon Scoresheet
options.lineage: jet-age ticket wallet, fused with the club scoresheet's carbon duplicate
options.thesis: Each game is a carbon scoresheet; the review stamps itself onto it and nothing ever disappears.
options.viewport: Review: the scoresheet's numbered move rows run beside the board, errors are struck in carbon red, and result and accuracy are boxed at the foot like a signed sheet.
options.case: Fuses well, because players sign a carbon scoresheet after every over-the-board game, but it loses narrowly on clarity for the pattern view.
options.risk: The form grid can feel bureaucratic and dense on a phone.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.thesis: Weaknesses as regions on a map.
options.viewport: Insights as a map of lobes.
options.risk: Club players don't identify with it, and it obscures the task.
options.kept: Region-scale colour commitment, for the lead divider on Insights.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: The game as a vertical score, white left and black right.
options.viewport: A centre staff of moves read upward.
options.risk: Unfamiliar reading direction for chess players.
options.kept: Length encodes real duration: time spent per move.

options.label: Lexicon Page
options.thesis: Black text, colour only inside plates.
options.risk: Too bookish for a fast analysis tool.
options.kept: Colour quarantine: quality colour only on marks and tabs.

options.label: Split-Flap Board
options.thesis: Games as departures, reviews flipping into place.
options.kept: A strict ruled ledger where state changes re-stamp rows in place.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.risk: Pure style with no tie to chess.
options.kept: One drawing repeated at many scales.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The familiar analysis board of chess.com and Lichess, executed with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Dark shell; eval bar and board at the left; move table and engine lines at the right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the sites it reviews, by design.
